_authority: How much theory a module carries, and how much must be taught before a trainee is asked anything (L36). Read by scripts/content_script.py (Stage 3 - every finding is shown on the review page and must be fixed before approval, unless the operator approves despite it, L26) and scripts/make_architecture_page.py (Stage 2 - whether the planned self-checks fit the module's theory time). Change a number here and both follow. The writer's rules that use them are in script/GUIDE.md; why each number is what it is: knowledge/HISTORY.md.

slide._merge_words: Two plain theory slides in a row on one Sub-ILO whose words together are this many or fewer (the slide's target) fit one slide: a note suggests the one slide.

module._plain_only: Counted over PLAIN theory only - the slides without "active".

before_self_check._cycles: Short cycles: about 5 minutes of theory, then the trainees do something. Active slides count as theory taught here.

self_check._rich: Rich is a task of the locate, operate, investigate or build family (media-and-tasks.json mechanics "family"), a scenario or a prediction (a choice with a consequence), or any question on a 3D model, an animation or a simulator. At most basic_max basic questions (the choose and arrange families), the rest rich up to rich_min. Always a must-fix: "basic_why" does not turn it into a note.

task_variety._what: Counted by family (media-and-tasks.json mechanics "family") in every set - each self-check, the module check, the final. No two neighbouring questions of one family - the note names the order that breaks the runs (a self-check keeps Part A before Part B where it can) or, when no order does, asks for another kind (content_script.py t_family_run); from from_questions questions on, no family takes more than max_family_share of the set (rounded to a whole question) and the set uses at least min_families families (t_family_share, t_few_families). Notes everywhere; task_plan.py plans the variety before the script is written.

task_plan._what: task_plan.py, printed by instructor_led.py plan before a module's script is written: per Sub-ILO a self-check kind (rich from challenge_from_level up) and a module-check kind of another family, the families its task type prefers and the ones least used in the module first, one that reaches the Sub-ILO's Bloom level (bloom.json ceiling); one challenge mechanic (media-and-tasks.json part) where a Sub-ILO asks Apply or higher; the module check's slots in an order with no two neighbours of one family. The equipment mechanics only for Sub-ILOs whose task type is done with the hands. The writer fills the slots; another kind of the same family is fine.

team_task._what: One team task a module where a Sub-ILO asks for Bloom 3 or higher, in place of one self-check's Part B: a task slide with "team": {"size", "roles", "scope"} that opens its own set (TT1, TT2 ...). Module checks and finals stay individual. It follows its self-check, so it is held to no self-check size (min_questions) or theory-first rule (before_self_check) and is no block of its own for spacing. A note when a module of from_module_minutes or more has none (content_script.py t_no_team).

recap._what: L51: every teaching module closes with ONE recap slide - "what to take away" - straight before the task slide that opens the module check, in the same animated design in every module (course-module-ui gb_compose.css section 11, markup in course-module-ux build/GUIDE.md). In the script it is a slide with "recap": true; its text is the points, one line each, "Short title - one sentence". Its visual_kind is none - the design is the picture. It is checked by its points, not by slide.target_words; its notes are checked like every slide's.

split._authority: The programme's hours never change (L1); what changes is how the class spends them. Measured on the Stage 2 page and every Stage 3 review page. A suggestion, not a rule.
split._keep_theory: The target is reached with TIME, never by cutting theory: every good theory slide stays (more may be added), its minutes shrink and the minutes it frees go to active learning. No suggestion ever says to remove a slide or cut its teaching: words that leave the screen go to the instructor (short points, the full text to the panel; or the notes' Say:), never out of the module. The density floor still applies.
split._counts: PLAIN = minutes of slides without "active" (the instructor explaining). ACTIVE = slides with "active" (one of the techniques below) + task slides (self-checks, module check, team tasks) + activities (practice, simulator, equipment). Stage 2: plain = the module's theory minutes less its self-checks, module check and the planned theory-as-activity minutes; active = those + the programme's practical minutes.
split._techniques: What makes a SLIDE active - the trainees do something on it, not only listen: explain-then-reveal (they explain first, then the slide shows it), predict-then-reveal (they predict what happens, then see), worked-example (one worked through, then their own attempt), scenario (what would you do), explore (they work the interactive diagram or 3D model themselves - turn it, open it, find the part). The instructor notes say what the trainees do. Marking a slide active that is only shown is not allowed: the operator reads it on the review page.

tablets._law: L35. The course runs on two tablets.
tablets.instructor_tablet: Shows the slides; the instructor terminal mirrors them to the classroom screen through the web view. The instructor notes are on the instructor's panel only. When it is time for a task, the slide on the screen only says that a task starts now and what it is about - the task itself is never on a slide - and the instructor's panel carries one button, OPEN TASK.
tablets.trainee_tablet: Carries only tasks: self-checks, the module check and the final assessment. A task opens on every trainee tablet automatically when the instructor presses OPEN TASK - and only then. The trainee cannot see a list of tasks, cannot browse or open another task, and there is no 'all tasks', 'module tasks' or 'back to tasks' button. One question per screen, Next -> Next; at the end the trainee sees their own score.
tablets.scores: Self-check: the trainee sees their own score, no pass mark. Module check: the score only, no pass mark and no verdict - its words say 'You see how many you got right - it shows what to review, it is not a grade.' The final assessment is the only official grade.
